title: Sicily + Rome · Ionian Coast + Eternal City — June 2027

packing: Real layers for Etna: the summit runs 20–30°F colder than the coast with strong sun — pack fleece, windbreakers and closed shoes for all four.
Water shoes: Isola Bella and Mazzarò are pebble beaches; Fontane Bianche is the sandy exception.
International Driving Permit: required alongside a U.S. license to drive in Italy — get both adults’ IDPs from AAA before departure.

days.heading: Arrive, drive to Ortigia + unpack

days.note: Arrive Fri Jun 11. Collect an automatic car, drive about an hour to Ortigia, unpack and eat locally. No timed sightseeing after the overnight flight.

days.heading: Ortigia: market, Duomo + sea decks
days.daycost: Est. $140 · market lunch, castle entry, dinner
days.note: Morning market and Duomo piazza while it’s cool, Borderi sandwiches for lunch, a sea-deck swim in the afternoon and the Maniace point for sunset.

spots.cost: The island, Duomo piazza, market and sea decks are free to wander. Castello Maniace is about $9 adults / under-18 free (closed Monday); a one-hour sea-cave boat runs about $22–28 per person — verify both prices for 2027.
spots.climate: About 64–83°F air; Ionian water near 73°F. Swim off the Ortigia sea decks or Cala Rossa in the calm morning, then retreat to shade or the apartment through the hottest early afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Build lunch from Caseificio Borderi sandwiches at the market and keep the sea decks and passeggiata as the free anchors.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the one-hour sea-cave boat from the marina on a calm morning and book a waterfront-adjacent apartment with AC and four real beds.
spots.restoHtml:
• Schiticchio — Ortigia’s go-to wood-fired pizza; plain Margherita on the menu
  • Caseificio Borderi — legendary market sandwiches made to order at lunch
  • Il Veliero — rustic family seafood spot with plain pasta for the kids
  • Keep breakfast fruit, granita stops and gelato in the daily plan — that is the local rhythm.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sea-deck swim + gelato loop when the day gets too hot for sights.
  • Aretusa spring + puppet museum for a low-output cultural hour.

days.note: Be at Neapolis for opening before the heat, then rest at the apartment through midday and give Noto the late afternoon — granita at Caffè Sicilia, photos when the limestone glows.

spots.cost: Parco Neapolis (Greek Theatre) is about $15 adults / $8 reduced at the official park tariff. Noto and Marzamemi cost nothing to walk. In June the INDA festival dresses the ancient theatre in wooden staging and closes it mid-afternoon on performance days — check the 2027 calendar before picking the morning.
spots.climate: Noto’s stone streets radiate heat by midday. Do the theatre and Noto in the morning, take the beach or pool break in the afternoon, and save golden-hour photos for after 5pm when the limestone glows.
spots.saveHtml: Save Combine the theatre with free Noto strolling and a Fontane Bianche beach afternoon; skip paid add-ons entirely.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book evening INDA festival seats — a Greek tragedy at sunset in the original theatre is a once-in-a-childhood upgrade if the 2027 dates line up.
spots.restoHtml:
• Caffè Sicilia — Noto’s famous granita and pastry stop on the main corso
  • Marzamemi piazza trattorias — casual pasta and pizza tables on the fishing-village square
  • Pack water and snacks — the archaeological park has little shade and simple kiosks.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Fontane Bianche beach replaces the afternoon if the kids are templed-out.
  • Vendicari reserve boardwalk for flamingos and an easy nature hour in the cooler evening.

days.note: Pack up after breakfast, drive the autostrada north, drop bags at the Giardini Naxos base and spend the afternoon on Isola Bella’s famous pebble causeway.

days.heading: Etna summit day
days.feel: The volcano the kids will remember
days.daycost: Est. $380 · cable car + jeep, lunch, granita
days.note: Drive the south slope to Rifugio Sapienza, ride the cable car (and 4x4 if conditions allow) toward the summit craters, then decompress with Alcantara’s cold river or Zafferana granita on the way down.

spots.cost: From Rifugio Sapienza the cable car is about $59 adults / $33 child 5–10 round trip; cable car plus 4x4 jeep to ~2,900m is about $86 adults / $55 child at the March 2026 tariff — roughly $310 for this family. The Silvestri craters at the parking lot are free.
spots.climate: Expect 20–30°F colder than the coast, strong sun and loose ash. Bring real layers, closed shoes and sunglasses for everyone; the upper mountain closes on volcanic-activity or wind warnings, so treat the jeep stage as conditional.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride only the cable car — or just walk the free Silvestri craters — and picnic from the Ortigia market instead of the mountain cafeterias.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the 4x4 + guide stage to ~2,900m for the closest family-legal look at the summit craters, and cap the day with granita in Zafferana Etnea.
spots.restoHtml:
• Passopomo — farm-to-table trattoria and pizza on the Zafferana slope
  • Zafferana Etnea gelaterias — the granita-and-brioche stop on the way down.
  • Mountain cafeterias at Sapienza are basic; a packed lunch beats them.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Gole dell’Alcantara ($2 municipal stairs or $14/$10 botanical park) for a cold-river canyon hour on the drive back.
  • Silvestri craters only if wind or activity closes the upper mountain — still a real volcano day.

days.heading: Taormina town + theatre
days.daycost: Est. $220 · theatre, cable car, boat or dinner
days.note: Teatro Antico early with Etna framed in the arches, corso wandering and granita, then a Mazzarò swim or the coast boat before the one dress-up dinner of the trip.

spots.cost: Teatro Antico is about $15 adults / $8 reduced (open to ~19:45 daily). Isola Bella’s reserve entry is about $4.50, the town cable car $7 one-way / $11 round trip, and a two-hour coast boat with swim stops runs about $33–50 per person — all 2025/2026 tariffs to recheck.
spots.climate: About 61–77°F with sea water near 72–74°F. The pebble beaches need water shoes; mornings are calmer for the boat and the theatre is most photogenic (and coolest) right after opening or before close.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride the cable car down to Mazzarò, swim the free public stretch beside Isola Bella and picnic on the beach.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the two-hour coast boat around Isola Bella’s grottoes, then a corso passeggiata dinner — Taormina is the trip’s one dress-up evening.
spots.restoHtml:
• Vecchia Taormina — wood-fired pizza just off the corso; plain pies and fries
  • Al Saraceno — terrace pizza with Etna views; breaded chicken for picky kids
  • La Bussola — Giardini Naxos waterfront pizzeria-grill near the base
  • Granita at a corso café counts as breakfast here — lean in.
spots.altboxHtml:
• Beach-only day at Mazzarò if the town crowds are heavy (mid-June is film-festival season).
  • Giardini Naxos promenade evening for a calmer, cheaper dinner than the corso.

days.feel: A real holiday, with no packing until evening
days.daycost: Public beach free; lido or boat costs use the activity allowance.

facts.label: PTO

days.note: Repeat the best beach, book a weather-dependent short boat ride or spend the day at the pool. Keep Etna movable into this slot if wind or volcanic restrictions close the earlier outing.

days.heading: Catania → Rome; settle into the city

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: Allow 5–6 hours door to door, including car return and baggage

days.note: Return the car at CTA, take a daytime nonstop to FCO and transfer to an air-conditioned apartment near the historic center. This is a separate trip leg, four days before the flight home; never a same-day self-transfer.

days.heading: Colosseum morning, lazy afternoon
days.daycost: Current basic admission: €18/adult; under-18 admission free, reservations and ID required.

facts.label: Pace
facts.valueHtml: Early timed entry; stop after 2–3 hours if the children fade

days.note: Book the official timed entry when the date releases. Choose a short Forum route rather than trying to cover the entire archaeological park. Apartment rest after lunch, then an easy dinner.

spots.cost: Current base family admission €36 before any optional extras; recheck 2027 tariff.
spots.climate: Rome June planning proxy: roughly 61–83°F. Midday heat can exceed the average; use AC breaks. No natural swimming scheduled in Rome.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the official basic ticket; save the arena and underground upgrade for a trip where everyone wants it.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A short private family guide instead of a full-day tour; quote before booking.
spots.restoHtml:
• Dar Poeta, Trastevere — Margherita, marinara and fries on the current menu.
  • Tonnarello, Trastevere — pasta and pizza; request simple sauce and check the current menu. Plan an early meal to avoid a long queue.
spots.altboxHtml:

  • Use a grocery picnic or plain takeaway pizza if restaurant waiting is tiring.

Sicily + Rome

Open jaw into Catania, home from Rome

International · $6,800–$8,800 allowance

Search PIT → CTA Jun 10 / FCO → PIT Jun 23 as one protected multi-city ticket. This exact route has not been quoted for four. The repository’s Nov 3 Sicily snapshot was $6,144 for Jun 12–20; a current separate-date Rome search lists $1,240/person for Jun 12–19. Neither establishes this open-jaw fare.

Catania → Rome · Jun 19

Ryanair currently advertises June 2027 fares from €36.29 one way. That is a monthly fare floor, not four seats on Jun 19. Budget $450–$850 for four including baggage/seat reserve; compare ITA and total checkout cost. Current flying time is about 1h25. Exact flight time and inventory remain unknown.

Sicily + Rome

One island car; Rome on foot and by taxi

Sicily · about 8 rental days

Collect CTA Jun 11; return CTA Jun 19. Ortigia to Naxos is about 1h45; Naxos to CTA about an hour. Keep the IDP, insurance and ZTL/parking checks from the Sicily plan. Car and insurance are unquoted allowances.

Rome · no rental

Allow $400–$650 for airport access, urban transport and heat-saving taxis. Budget extra time for the Saturday arrival. Walking plans are deliberately short; four flights of stairs or distant lodging can undo that benefit.

Recommendation: keep Sicily + Rome as the baseline. This is a proposed decision rule, not a priced upgrade. Do not buy a nonrefundable Venice stay before the VCE return works.

Sicily + Rome

Heat, Etna and tickets set the order

Heat management

Rome in June needs early starts and afternoon AC. Sicily has warm water, pebble entries and a pool fallback. Pack water shoes, hats, refill bottles and Etna layers.

Etna + wildfire

The inherited Sicily June fire planning band is moderate, 5–10%, not a forecast. Follow official daily alerts and airport/volcano restrictions. Keep Jun 18 as the recovery slot.

Book the right ticket

Official Colosseum tickets: current base €18/adult, under-18s free but still require the appropriate reservation and ID. 2027 release rules must be rechecked. Trevi’s basin currently costs €2/person; viewing from the square stays the simple fallback.

Sicily + Rome

Return June 23; a week later does not fit

Jun 10 is Thursday; Jun 18 is the observed Juneteenth Friday. Counting the departure day, this window uses nine weekdays after that holiday. If your employer does not observe it, count ten. An evening departure could reduce nine to eight only after flight timings are confirmed. Moving one week later would overlap the required full Pittsburgh days Jun 24–26; use an earlier departure or a later post-commitment window instead.
